card.name: Verb after a drug class in warnings
card.fires_on: The verb right after a drug or drug class as subject in a warning, such as "has", "have" or "shown", just before "been associated with" or "an increased risk". Also "patients" after "In some".

modes.label: Has/have before been associated
modes.description: Helper verb after a drug or class name, leading into reported associations with rare reactions.
modes.example: Use of TNF blockers, of which CIMZIA is a member,<< has>> been associated with rare cases of new onset

modes.label: Trials have shown
modes.description: The verb "shown" after clinical trials, leading into a reported risk.
modes.example: 1 Cardiovascular Thrombotic Events Clinical trials of several COX-2 selective and nonselective NSAIDs of up to three years duration have<< shown>> an increased risk of serious cardiovascular (CV

modes.label: In some patients
modes.description: The word "patients" after "In some", introducing an effect seen only in certain people.
modes.example: Inhibitors - In some<< patients>>, the administration of a non-ster

card.writes: It promotes words meaning "certain" or "some", suggesting a hedged statement about only some cases follows.
card.plain: It marks the verb in warnings that say a drug has been linked to or shown a problem in some patients.
